note: prop_chose_higher_ev 0.78 IS NOT EXTRACTED FROM THE CITED PAPER. Ciranka, S. & van den Bos, W. (2025), 'Internal uncertainty impacts social information use in risky choice across adolescence', Communications Psychology 3:137, doi:10.1038/s44271-025-00314-6, reports the proportion of RISKY choices under its experimental manipulations, modelled with a Bayesian GLMM; it does not report a proportion of expected-value-maximising choices, which is what this port scores. SAMPLE MISMATCH, and it is the reason to be careful here: the study is developmental. N=166 German participants aged 10-26 (mean 15.82, SD 5.13; 76 female, 90 male), recruited in Berlin, 144 trials. Its central finding is that adolescents differ from both children and adults in risk-taking and in susceptibility to social information, so a single pooled figure from this sample is NOT an adult baseline and should not be presented as one. TASK CORRESPONDENCE, verified: the safe jar always pays 5 points; the risky jar pays 8, 20 or 50 points with probability 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625 or 0.75. Expected value is therefore well defined per trial and the port's higher-EV metric is computable, but the paper simply never publishes that quantity. Obtaining it needs the trial-level data (preregistration: osf.io/nsy69).
